outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the only new event that claims to settle the bullet is a single-author Zenodo preprint (published 17 January 2026) asserting a complete resolution by differential-algebraic methods; I read its landing page and abstract but not its PDF, and I found no public engagement with it in about nine months. Everything else in the window is a different question (generalised or universal quadratic forms over number fields) or an unrelated AI-assisted paper. The older record (Hasse 1924 for equivalence over number fields; Kneser, Duke–Schulze-Pillot and Cogdell's 2003 account for integral representation in special cases) predates the window and is recorded below.
problem_asks: The bullet as worded in the frozen revision: 'Hilbert's eleventh problem: classify quadratic forms over algebraic number fields.' Unpacked: (a) the objects are quadratic forms whose coefficients lie in an algebraic number field K; (b) the range is every algebraic number field K and every dimension n of such forms; (c) the ask is a classification, meaning a criterion or complete list of invariants that decides when two such forms are equivalent (isometric) over K. The bullet's wording does not mention integers, rings of integers, or representing numbers. Those belong to Hilbert's 1900 formulation, which the Wikipedia article gives as asking whether a quadratic equation with algebraic coefficients can be solved 'by integral or fractional numbers belonging to the algebraic realm of rationality determined by the coefficients'. I record that original wording as context, not as part of problem_asks. Whether the bullet asks for (c) alone or also for the integral/representation question is a call for the judging pass, and the competing_reading field sets out both sides.

events.what_happened: Hasse's doctoral dissertation (1921), 'Über die Darstellbarkeit von Zahlen durch quadratische Formen im Körper der rationalen Zahlen', develops the local-global principle over the rational field. MacTutor says Hasse discovered the principle in October 1920, at Hensel's suggestion, and that Hensel replied by pointing out its deeper meaning. Recorded for completeness: it is the rational-field case, which the bullet's generalisation to arbitrary number fields goes beyond.
events.delivers: Local-global criterion for representing rational numbers by rational quadratic forms. Base field Q only; representation rather than equivalence of forms.
events.remains: All of the bullet for general number fields, and the classification of forms over Q, which the Wikipedia article credits to Minkowski's earlier work.

checked_by.qualification: Hasse's supervisor, originator of p-adic methods
checked_by.what_they_did: Replied to Hasse's result and pointed out its deeper meaning (a ternary form with a nontrivial zero over every completion has one over the rationals), per MacTutor

events.direction: Affirmative for the rational-field case of representability.

events.what_happened: Hasse, 'Äquivalenz quadratischer Formen in einem beliebigen algebraischen Zahlkörper', Crelle's Journal 153 (1924). The title is as given in Roquette's transcription of Hasse's bibliography, which I saw only in a search snippet and did not open. The paper establishes the local-global principle for equivalence of quadratic forms over an arbitrary algebraic number field. The Wikipedia article (opened) says Hasse 'solved' the problem with his local-global principle and dates the publications to 1923 and 1924; the sentence is garbled in the fetched text. A companion paper on representing numbers by forms over number fields also appears in Crelle 153 (snippet only).
events.delivers: For nondegenerate quadratic forms over any algebraic number field K: two forms are equivalent over K exactly when they are equivalent over every completion of K. Per a survey summary in a search snippet (not opened), this is the local-global principle for equivalence. It gives a classification up to isometry in terms of local invariants. It does not, on its face, address forms over rings of integers, classes within genera, or representation of integers.
events.remains: Integral classification (forms over rings of integers, class and genus questions) and the representation of integers by forms, which Wikipedia names as Hilbert's focus. Whether the bullet's wording requires these is for the judging pass.

checked_by.qualification: Algebraist who wrote on quadratic forms and reviewed Hasse's collected work
checked_by.what_they_did: Described the 1923–1924 papers as 'five beautiful papers on quadratic forms' (quoted in a search snippet; not opened)

events.doubts: None raised in the sources. Note that the Wikipedia sentence about Hasse's status is garbled in the text I fetched, and the 1924 title is from a transcription I did not open.
events.direction: Affirmative for the literal wording of the bullet: it gives a complete local criterion for equivalence of forms over any number field.

events.what_happened: Kneser, 'Klassenzahlen indefiniter quadratischer Formen in drei oder mehr Veränderlichen', Arch. Math. 7 (1956), 323–332. Cited from secondary references; the paper itself was not opened. Per those references, Kneser computes local spinor norms, which gives one class per genus for indefinite forms in the relevant cases, over the rational integers. Blomer and Harcos (opened) list 'the indefinite case and the positive definite case with n ⩾ 4 (Siegel, Kneser, Hsia, and others)' as already settled, but I could not verify the years of the Siegel and Hsia contributions.
events.delivers: Integral local-to-global behaviour for indefinite integral forms in three or more variables, via spinor norms, with class number one of the genus in the relevant cases. Per secondary sources, over the rational integers. The number-field version is credited to Siegel, Kneser, Hsia and others in the Blomer–Harcos introduction, but I did not read those sources.
events.remains: Positive definite forms in dimension three; the number-field versions beyond what Blomer–Harcos cite; definite cases generally.

checked_by.who: Valentin Blomer and Gergely Harcos (as citing authors)
checked_by.qualification: Analytic number theorists writing a refereed paper on the same question
checked_by.what_they_did: Cite the indefinite case, and the positive definite case with n ⩾ 4, as settled by Siegel, Kneser, Hsia and others in the introduction of their 2009 preprint

events.direction: Affirmative for the indefinite integral case in dimension three and up, as far as it goes.

events.what_happened: Hsia, 'Representations by spinor genera' (1976), cited in a secondary reference list; the paper was not opened. Per the abstract text in a search snippet: for integral forms over a fixed domain of algebraic integers with dim(f) − dim(g) ≥ 2, if f represents g over every p-adic field and over the reals, then the genus of f represents g; the abstract then asks how many spinor genera in the genus represent g. Hsia's 1975 paper on spinor norms of local integral rotations is cited alongside.
events.delivers: Per the snippet: a local-to-genus statement for integral representations over a fixed ring of algebraic integers with dimension gap at least 2. The spinor-genus count is posed as a question in the abstract.
events.remains: The count of spinor genera representing g, as the abstract itself poses it.
events.doubts: Only a snippet of the abstract was seen; the full theorem was not read.
events.direction: Refines the integral picture; does not decide the representation question for all forms.

events.what_happened: Duke and Schulze-Pillot, 'Representation of integers by positive ternary quadratic forms and equidistribution of lattice points on ellipsoids', Invent. Math. 99 (1990), 49–57 (Zbl 0692.10020). The full text was not opened. Per a Zentralblatt review quoted in a search snippet, all sufficiently large integers primitively represented by the spinor genus of a positive ternary form f are represented by f itself. Blomer and Harcos (opened) state that the positive definite ternary case was 'solved by Duke and Schulze-Pillot' for K = Q.
events.delivers: Positive definite integral ternary quadratic forms over Q: for sufficiently large integers primitively represented by the spinor genus, the form itself represents them. Restricted to Q, to large integers, and to primitive representations.
events.remains: Small integers, non-primitive representations, and every number field other than Q, which Cogdell–Piatetski-Shapiro–Sarnak cover for totally real fields (see the 2003 event).

checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote the review quoted in a snippet, which states the main theorem and the spinor-exceptional complication

checked_by.who: Valentin Blomer and Gergely Harcos (as citing authors)
checked_by.what_they_did: State the Q-case as solved by Duke and Schulze-Pillot in their introduction

events.direction: Affirmative for the representation question in the positive definite ternary case over Q, for large integers.

events.what_happened: A 2002 University of Pennsylvania lecture announcement, reported in search snippets as saying that recent progress has led to the solution of Hilbert's eleventh problem, framed as representability of integers by quadratic forms over a number field. The page (math.upenn.edu/node/8986) could not be opened: the fetch failed with a certificate error. The speaker is not confirmed; one search summary attributes the abstract to Peter Sarnak, which I did not verify.
events.delivers: Not established. This is a talk abstract, and the sources I reached give no written argument for the claim.
events.remains: All of it, as far as the sources show.
events.time_since_posted: not established; no written argument located, so engagement with the claim could not be checked
events.doubts: A talk abstract, not a written argument. The 'solution' claim is stated without mathematics in the sources I could reach. Per §5.1 it should be dated to a write-up, and I did not find one.
events.direction: Claims a solution in the representability sense; no object or argument given.

events.what_happened: Cogdell, 'On sums of three squares', J. Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux 15 (2003), 33–44. The paper is an exposition of joint work with Piatetski-Shapiro and Sarnak; the joint paper is cited there as 'in preparation'. The abstract (opened) says that for positive definite integral ternary forms over a totally real field, every sufficiently large totally positive squarefree integer is globally integrally represented if and only if it is locally represented at all places, and calls this 'essentially resolving the remaining open case of Hilbert's eleventh problem'. I could not locate the joint paper itself or its date.
events.revisions: The joint CPS paper is cited as 'in preparation' in 2003 and I found no published version. Harcos's slides (snippet) attribute a subconvexity exponent to CPS 2000, which is a different estimate. The date given is the earliest written account I could open, not a date for the joint argument.
events.delivers: For positive definite integral ternary forms over a totally real field K: each sufficiently large totally positive squarefree integer (norm above an ineffective bound c) is globally represented if and only if it is locally represented at every completion. Restrictions: ternary, positive definite, totally real K, squarefree, totally positive, large with an ineffective constant. Cogdell's own qualifier is 'essentially resolving'.
events.remains: Non-squarefree integers (which Blomer–Harcos call 'subtler' and handle by citing other work); an effective constant; forms of rank other than three; fields that are not totally real.

checked_by.qualification: Automorphic-forms researcher and one of the joint authors of the underlying analytic estimates
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote a published exposition of the ideas behind the joint proof. This is an exposition, not a verification of the full joint paper.

events.doubts: The joint CPS argument was not read. Cogdell's text is an exposition and does not itself verify the joint paper. The ineffective constant limits the statement, which is a scope point rather than a doubt about correctness.
events.direction: Affirmative for the totally real ternary positive definite case, for large squarefree totally positive integers. Does not reach non-squarefree integers or forms of other ranks.

events.what_happened: Peter Sarnak's IAS lecture 'Solutions to Equations in Integers', listed for 26 March 2008 (date and speaker from a search snippet). The IAS page returned HTTP 403 to my fetch, so the abstract is seen only in a snippet. The snippet says that Hilbert's 11th problem 'complete solution relies on recent advances in related fields as well as many developments over the years'.
events.delivers: Not established. This is a talk description with no argument.
events.remains: All of it, as far as the sources show.
events.time_since_posted: not applicable; no written argument located
events.doubts: A talk description only. The sentence describes how a solution depends on other developments; it is not a stated result.
events.direction: No direction on the bullet; a descriptive statement about the problem's history.

events.what_happened: Blomer and Harcos, 'Twisted L-functions over number fields and Hilbert's eleventh problem', arXiv:0904.2429 (v1 16 April 2009; v2 1 May 2009; v3 13 October 2009), published in Geom. Funct. Anal. 20 (2010), 1–52 (DOI 10.1007/s00039-010-0063-x, from a search snippet). The abstract (opened) says: 'We prove a Burgess-like subconvex bound for twisted L-functions of a fixed irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of GL(2) over a totally real number field', proved via a spectral decomposition of shifted convolution sums and a generalized Kuznetsov formula. The introduction (opened) states the problem as 'which integers are integrally represented by a given' quadratic form, and says the paper's Corollary 2 gives asymptotic formulae for representations of totally positive integers by positive integral ternary forms over totally real K. It does not claim to settle the problem; its stated improvement over CPS is a sharper error term, 'not a new local-global principle'.
events.revisions: v1 16 Apr 2009; v2 1 May 2009 (introduction revised); v3 13 Oct 2009 (small corrections). Published in GAFA 2010 (search snippet). An erratum dated 1 Nov 2013 is posted on Harcos's website, correcting several points including a bundle-triviality argument and some normalisations (search snippet; not opened).
events.delivers: A subconvexity bound for twisted GL(2) L-functions over totally real fields. As applications, a sharper count of representations of squarefree totally positive integers of norm at least c by positive ternary integral forms over K (Corollary 2), with the local-global input credited to CPS. Establishes no local-global principle and no classification.
events.remains: The whole bullet. The paper's own scope is an analytic error term in a representation count, not the classification or the representation question.

checked_by.what_they_did: Published in Geometric and Functional Analysis (refereed), with a 2013 erratum

events.doubts: The 2013 erratum corrects several points, including a bundle-triviality argument (snippet only; not opened). No other concern appears in the sources.
events.direction: Moves an auxiliary bound (an L-function subconvexity exponent) and an error term in a representation count. The problem's status is unchanged according to the paper's own introduction.

events.what_happened: Xu and Zhang, 'On indefinite and potentially universal quadratic forms over number fields', arXiv:2004.02090 (v1 5 April 2020; v2 21 May 2020; v3 1 November 2021). No journal reference is listed on the arXiv page. The paper gives class-number criteria: a number field admits a binary integral form that is locally but not globally universal iff its class number exceeds one (finitely many classes); a ternary such form exists iff the class number is even (infinitely many classes); and for forms in more than one variable, representing every integer of the field is equivalent to representing 1 over the ring of integers.
events.delivers: Criteria for locally-but-not-globally universal integral forms over number fields. The question is universality, a different question from classification of forms or representation of a given integer.
events.time_since_posted: not assessed; discounted as a different question, and no engagement search was run
events.doubts: Engagement with this preprint was not assessed. It is discounted only because it is about universal forms.
events.direction: Does not bear on the bullet's direction; a different question (universality).

events.what_happened: He, Hu and Xu, 'On indefinite k-universal integral quadratic forms over number fields', arXiv:2201.10730 (v1 26 January 2022; v2 12 May 2022), published in Math. Z. 304 (2023), no. 1, article 20 (DOI 10.1007/s00209-023-03280-z, from the arXiv journal reference). The abstract (opened) says that for k ≥ 3 the indefinite k-universal property satisfies the local-global principle over number fields; for k = 2 a number field has a locally 2-universal but not indefinite 2-universal lattice exactly when its class number is even; and for k = 1 gives a criterion involving dyadic primes.
events.revisions: v1 26 Jan 2022; v2 12 May 2022 (terminology changed; Section 6 strengthened). Journal: Math. Z. 304 (2023).
events.delivers: Local-global and class-number criteria for k-universal indefinite lattices over number fields. The question is universality, not classification or representation of a given integer.
events.direction: Does not bear on the bullet's direction; a different question (k-universal forms).

events.what_happened: Browning, Pierce and Schindler, 'Generalised quadratic forms over totally real number fields', arXiv:2212.11038, first posted December 2022 (per the journal's pages in search results; the arXiv page was not opened). Published in J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 23 (2024), no. 6, 2859–2912 (DOI 10.1017/S1474748024000161; online 11 April 2024). Per the search snippets, the paper introduces a new class of generalised quadratic forms over totally real number fields, rich enough to capture arbitrary systems of quadrics over Q, and uses a number-field version of the Hardy–Littlewood circle method.
events.revisions: arXiv December 2022; journal received 4 Jan 2023, revised 29 Feb 2024, accepted 5 Mar 2024, published online 11 Apr 2024 (per the journal record in a snippet).
events.delivers: A new class of generalised quadratic forms and a circle-method count over totally real number fields. The question is counting rational points on systems of quadrics, not classifying forms or representing integers.

checked_by.who: Cambridge University Press peer review (J. Inst. Math. Jussieu)
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted after revision on 5 March 2024 (per the journal's submission record in a snippet)

events.direction: Does not bear on the bullet's direction; a different question (counting).

events.what_happened: Chwiedziuk, Doležálek, Pěchoučková, Pezlar, Prakash, Romeo, Růžičková and Zindulka, 'Representing rational integers by generalized quadratic forms over quadratic fields', arXiv:2403.07171, first submitted 11 March 2024 (v2 21 March 2026). The arXiv abstract (opened) says the paper investigates generalized quadratic forms with values in the rational integers over quadratic fields; it characterises the real quadratic fields admitting a positive definite binary generalized form that represents every positive integer, and shows that only finitely many fields admit a ternary generalized form with these properties. A journal version appears in the New York Journal of Mathematics 32 (2026) (search snippet; not opened).

events.what_happened: Shifa Liu (single listed author; the Zenodo record gives a Peking University affiliation), 'A Differential-Algebraic Resolution of Hilbert's Eleventh Problem: Towards a Paradigm Shift in Analytic Computation', posted to Zenodo as a version-1 preprint (hilbert_11th.pdf, 644.7 kB, 43 pages, CC BY 4.0) and mirrored on the Synapse aggregator. The Zenodo abstract (opened) says: 'This paper presents a comprehensive differential-algebraic framework for Hilbert's eleventh problem'. It constructs differentially closed field extensions for quadratic forms over number fields and gives algorithms based on local conditions to decide whether a quadratic form globally represents zero. It states: 'The solution addresses all remaining aspects of the problem.' The Synapse abstract (opened) says the framework 'restores formal decidability for a broad class of Diophantine problems constrained by local conditions' and 'explicitly distinguish[es] the decidable problem of rational points from the undecidable problem of integer points'. The PDF was not read: WebFetch returned compressed bytes, and a text-extraction command was not approved. The theorems, proof and acknowledgements are therefore unverified.
events.revisions: Zenodo lists one version (v1, published 17 January 2026); its page gives a submission date of 31 December 2025. The Synapse page is dated 20 January 2026 and cites the work as (2025). The Zenodo abstract says the work resolves 'all identified issues in previous versions', but no earlier version is listed. The Synapse page gives DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18281104; the Zenodo record is 10.5281/zenodo.18281105. The DOI 18281104 resolves to the same record.
events.delivers: From the abstract only, and not verified: a decision method for whether a quadratic form over a number field globally represents zero, from local conditions; and a claimed decidability result for the rational-point version of the problem, contrasted with undecidability for the integer-point version. Whether the claimed scope covers all forms over all number fields, and whether it covers the integral representation question, cannot be read from the abstract.
events.remains: By the abstract's own account, nothing: it claims to address 'all remaining aspects'. But it also says the integer-point problem is undecidable, which, on the abstract's own terms, is a negative answer for that part rather than a classification of it. The parts already in Hasse–Minkowski theory (local-global equivalence over number fields, Hasse 1924) are not shown to be extended.
events.directly_checkable: Not established. The abstract claims explicit algorithms for deciding whether a quadratic form globally represents zero. I saw no worked example, and the PDF was not readable.
events.doubts: (1) Scope tension: the abstract says the integer-point version is undecidable and also that the work resolves 'all remaining aspects' of Hilbert's problem, whose original wording concerns solvability in integers or fractions of the field. The abstract does not say which of these it decides. (2) The rational-point decidability it advertises overlaps with classical Hasse–Minkowski theory, and the abstract does not say what is new. (3) Single preprint on Zenodo, unreviewed; the Synapse page says 'The Discussion section has no comments yet'; I found no journal submission, referee report, comment, blog discussion, or citing paper. (4) No Lean or Coq artifact found. (5) Version inconsistency: the abstract refers to fixes to 'previous versions', but only v1 is listed. (6) The abstract's framing ('paradigm shift in computational models', 'restores formal decidability') is not a stated theorem. (7) A Cambridge Engage posting on Hilbert's 13th problem and a Synapse listing on Hilbert's 21st problem, both seen only as search snippets, use closely parallel abstract wording. I could not establish whether they share an author, and I draw no conclusion from them. These are signals for the judging pass, not weighed here.
events.direction: Claims a complete resolution of the bullet, in the direction of a decision method for quadratic forms over number fields, while asserting undecidability for the integer-point version.

events.what_happened: Kramer and Krásenský, 'Non-universality of ternary quadratic forms over fields containing √2', arXiv:2601.15568, first submitted 22 January 2026 (single version). The arXiv abstract page (opened) says the paper proves Kitaoka's conjecture for all totally real number fields of degree 4, by showing that no positive definite classical ternary form is universal over them, focusing on fields containing √2, and also discusses lifting problems and criterion sets.
events.delivers: Non-existence of universal positive definite classical ternary forms over totally real quartic fields (Kitaoka's conjecture in degree 4). A universality question, not classification of forms or representation of a given integer.

disputes.summary: The sources disagree on the problem's status, and no named priority claimants conflict. The Wikipedia lead says Hasse solved it with his local-global principle (1923–1924) and notes later work by Cogdell, Piatetski-Shapiro and Sarnak. The Simons Foundation survey (Evelyn Lamb, 18 June 2026, opened) lists it as 'Resolved for some cases'. One search summary attributes 'partially solved' to the Encyclopedia of Mathematics; I did not find that entry. A 2002 Penn talk abstract (snippet only) says a solution has been reached. A 2017 arXiv survey of Hilbert problems in mathematical physics (snippet only) lists H11 as 'generally accepted as solved'. Liu's 2026 preprint claims 'all remaining aspects' are resolved, which none of the other sources says.

summary: Read against the bullet's literal wording, the record has one classical event that arguably settles it and one 2026 preprint that claims to settle the whole problem. Wikipedia's lead says Hasse solved the problem with his local-global principle; the 1924 Crelle paper on equivalence over an arbitrary number field gives equivalence over K as equivalence at all completions. I read that dating from Wikipedia and the Hasse biography, and the 1924 paper itself and its exact scope were not opened. Integral and representation questions are only partly answered: Kneser (1956), Siegel and Hsia handle indefinite forms and positive definite forms of dimension four or more (cited by Blomer–Harcos, with some dates unverified); Duke and Schulze-Pillot (1990) handle positive definite ternary forms over Q for large primitively represented integers; and Cogdell's 2003 account of the joint Cogdell–Piatetski-Shapiro–Sarnak work handles positive definite ternary forms over totally real fields for large squarefree totally positive integers, with an ineffective constant. Blomer and Harcos (2009), despite the title, prove a subconvexity bound and sharpen an error term; their introduction says they do not settle the problem. Inside the window the only claimed full resolution is Shifa Liu's Zenodo preprint (17 January 2026). I read its landing page and abstract but not its PDF. The abstract says 'The solution addresses all remaining aspects of the problem' and also that the integer-point problem is undecidable, which is a scope tension I could not resolve. I found no referee report, comment, citing paper, withdrawal or Lean artifact after about nine months. Other window events are different questions: Chwiedziuk et al. (generalised forms over quadratic fields, March 2024), Kramer–Krásenský (universal ternary forms over totally real quartic fields, January 2026), and Swaminathan (AI-assisted work on binary cubics, March 2026). Engagement with the discounted neighbours was not assessed. Close calls: whether the literal bullet counts as settled by Hasse in 1924 (see competing_reading); whether Liu's claim is in scope; and whether the Penn 2002 talk and IAS 2008 lecture count as claims (both are unopened talk descriptions). AI: no system is named in any source for any event bearing on this problem. The Liu landing page and abstract name none, but its PDF was not read, so AI disclosure in its acknowledgements is unverified. The one AI-assisted paper I found (Swaminathan) is about binary cubics, not this problem. The OpenAI 722-manuscript release (October 2026) has a Hilbert problem entry only for the tenth problem (family 004, over Q). I screened every 100k-character window of its CONTENTS.md by keyword and found no family on quadratic forms over number fields, though that screen was not a line-by-line read and the overview.pdf was not read. Among the other AI searches (AlphaEvolve/AlphaProof/Gemini, Claude/Anthropic, LLM terms, Lean/Mathlib), none linked the eleventh problem to a model. One non-AI observation: the Synapse page gives DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18281104, which resolves to the same record as 10.5281/zenodo.18281105.
competing_reading: Read literally, the bullet ('classify quadratic forms over algebraic number fields') was closed in 1924 by Hasse's local-global theorem for equivalence over any number field, so nothing in the window changes its status and Liu's preprint is irrelevant to the bullet's wording. The open residue is then Hilbert's integral and representation question (Wikipedia's 1900 wording), which the 2026 claim targets. In the other direction, a reader who takes Hilbert's original formulation and the Simons Foundation's 'Resolved for some cases' as the status would count the problem as partly open, and would count Liu only if its claim survives. Against counting Liu: no review, the PDF unread here, a scope tension in its own abstract, and no uptake for about nine months. For counting it: the abstract explicitly claims 'all remaining aspects' and the record gives no ground to reject it outright.
what_would_settle_it: (1) Reading the Liu PDF (hilbert_11th.pdf, 43 pages): its exact main theorem, whether it covers integral representation of integers as well as rational points, how it relates to Kneser, Siegel and Duke–Schulze-Pillot, and what its acknowledgements say about AI tools. (2) A referee report, a published comment, or a withdrawal on the Liu preprint, or confirmed silence after a longer period. (3) The 1924 Crelle paper's theorem statement for arbitrary number fields, to decide the literal-bullet reading. (4) The joint Cogdell–Piatetski-Shapiro–Sarnak paper, for its exact hypotheses and date. (5) The OpenAI CONTENTS.md and overview.pdf read line by line, to confirm there is no family on the eleventh problem.
